decisions.decision: Direct PS1 rate indexing for ADSR
decisions.rationale: Each fader position = one hardware rate, no interpolation — most faithful and eliminates all knob curve issues

decisions.decision: 5 separate measured tables per ADSR mode
decisions.rationale: Each mode (atk lin/exp, decay, rel lin/exp) produces different actual times; separate tables eliminate pre-warping math
PS1 spec gives 6.25% at level 0 but that prevents percussive hits; deliberate divergence for musical utility

decisions.decision: Vertical faders replace rotary encoders for ADSR
decisions.rationale: Long throw gives better resolution for stepping through discrete rates
Display was inaccurate; fader readouts give direct feedback

context_notes: Major ADSR rework this session. Root cause was timing tables using linear calculations while engine runs exponential (3-4x discrepancy). External AI reviews provided key insight: measure actual engine times, build separate tables per mode. Final architecture: 5 measured tables + direct index mapping + vertical faders. Attack still uses a piecewise knob curve for 0-25% percussive range while decay/release use pure direct indexing. Anthony approved attack and decay feel. Release got same curve as decay. Session paused mid-afternoon.
